ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
Since, this appeal and the cross-
objection

arise out of the same judgment and award dated 2.7.2019, passed by Jt. Civil Judge, Senior Division, Yavatmal (for short, "reference Court"), the appeal and the cross-objection are being disposed of by this common judgment.

2. I have heard learned advocate for appellant Mr. J.B. Kasat, learned advocate for respondent Nos.
1 and 2 Mr. A.B. Nakshane, and 4 fa970.2022_xob..odt learned AGP Ms. Deepa Charlewar for respondent Nos. 3 and 4/State.
3.
In this appeal, challenge is to the judgment and award dated 2.7.2019, passed by the reference Court, whereby the reference Court was pleased to partly allow the reference and grant enhancement.
The main grievance of the cross-objectors is that the irrigated land with the source of well water was treated as the seasonal irrigated land.
4. The land of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 bearing Gat No. 160/2, admeasuring 1.28 hector out of total land of 4.91 hector acquired for the purpose of Bembla main canal.
The notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 ("Act", for short) was published on 23.8.2007.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer ("SLAO", for short) passed the award on 26.8.2010.
The SLAO awarded the compensation @ Rs. 86,000/- (Rupees Eighty Six Thousand) per hector for acquired land and Rs. 1,46,736/- (Rupees One Lac Forty Six Thousand Seven Hundred Thirty Six) for well.

The reference Court enhanced the compensation of the land to 5 fa970.2022_xob..odt Rs. 7,15,590/-
(Rupees Seven Lac Fifteen Thousand Five Hundred Ninety) per hector and Rs. 1,76,100/- (Rupees One Lac Seventy Six Thousand One Hundred)for the well.
The appellant - the acquiring body is aggrieved by the enhancement granted by the reference Court.
Similarly, the cross-objectors being aggrieved by the inadequate enhancement, filed cross-objection to the appeal.
5. The claimants - cross-objectors filed reference contending that the compensation granted by the SLAO was not proper.
It is contended that the land was treated as seasonally irrigated land whereas the land is perennially irrigated land with source of well water.

6. The learned advocates for the parties have placed reliance on the decision of this Court in First Appeal No. 645/2019 (Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation and another Vs. Pushpabai Vasantrao Jadhao and others).

sentences.text:
It is pointed out that in this appeal, the compensation awarded in V. I. D. C. Through Executive Engineer, ... vs Kalanbi Rahemankhan Pathan And Others on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126478510/
3 respect of dry crop land was Rs. 4,77,059/- (Rupees Four Lac Seventy Seven Thousand Fifty Nine)
per hector.
The learned advocate submitted that except the dispute as to whether 6 fa970.2022_xob..odt the land is perennially irrigated or the seasonally irrigated, the appeal is covered by the judgment.

The learned advocate for the appellant submitted that considering the crop pattern and the evidence adduced before the reference Court, the reference Court was right in holding that the land was seasonally irrigated land.
The learned advocate for the appellant submitted that the evidence is not sufficient to prove that the land was perennially irrigated.
The learned advocate submitted that there is no evidence to prove that well was having the water to irrigate the land throughout the year.

As against this, the learned advocate for the claimants/cross-objectors submitted that the crop pattern may not be the sole decisive factor to decide whether the land is seasonally irrigated or perennially irrigated.
The learned advocate submitted that the 7/12 extract filed on record apart from indicating the crop pattern, suggests that the well had sufficient water for irrigating the land throughout the year.

The learned advocate took me through the report of the valuer and pointed out that at the time of inspection of the land on 15.4.2008, the valuer apart from recording the nature of the construction of well has noted down the depth of the well as well as depth of the available water.
Learned advocate 7 fa970.2022_xob..odt submitted that therefore, the reference Court was not right in rejecting this evidence.
7. The main question which needs to be addressed is whether the well had sufficient water for the purpose of irrigation of the land throughout the year.
The availability of water in the well, in my view, is the decisive factor.
The use of the available water depends upon the farmer.
The farmer may fall into two categories (i) idle and (ii) ideal.
The ideal farmer is bound to make the maximum use of the available water in the well.
As against this, the idle farmer despite having sufficient water, may not use it for any purpose.

Therefore, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has, time and again, held that crop pattern will not be the decisive factor to decide whether the land is seasonally irrigated or perennially irrigated without there being an availability of well water.
In this case, 7/12 extract filed on record indicate that the Kharip and Rabby crops were grown and the well water was used for irrigation.
The valuer in his report, has stated that the well was having the pakka construction in phadi, breaks and cement.
The well was having diameter of 5.50 meters, the depth was 13.10 meters and water 8 fa970.2022_xob..odt was available at the depth of 3.65 meters
. It means that on the date of inspection i.e. on 15.4.2008 at the beginning of the summer, actual depth of water was round 9 to 9.45 meters.
This shows that sufficient water was available in the well.

In my view, therefore,
the evidence on record is sufficient to conclude that the sufficient water was available in the well for making it available for the land in question throughout the year.
In the facts and circumstances, I am of the view that the learned reference Court has not properly appreciated these facts.
P.W. 1 in his evidence has stated that sufficient water is available in the well throughout the year.
In the facts and circumstances, I am of the view that to this extent, the reference Court was not right.
The evidence on record is sufficient to conclude that the land was perennially irrigated with the well water.
The compensation has been awarded for the well.
Out of total 4.91 hector land, 1.28 hector land with the well was acquired.
This indicate that after acquisition of land and well, the benefit of the water from the well is not available for the remaining land of the claimant.

In my view, therefore,
in this case, the cross- objectors are entitled to get compensation in respect of the acquired land holding it as a perennially irrigated land.

Accordingly, the appeal filed by the acquiring body - Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation is dismissed.
The cross-objection is partly allowed.

8. The claimants/cross objectors are entitled to get compensation @ Rs. 9,54,118/- (Rupees Nine Lacs Fifty Four Thousand One Hundred Eighteen) per hector with accrued interest alongwith other statutory benefits.
The claimants/cross-objectors are not entitled to get interest and other statutory benefits for the delay period caused in filing the cross-objection.
The amount of compensation awarded be 10 fa970.2022_xob..odt adjusted and accordingly, the balance amount be deposited within twelve weeks.
The First Appeal and the Cross-objection are disposed of in the above stated terms.
